claim: A book that comes back 30 days late is charged the 5.00 maximum fee.
why: The README says 0.25 per day, but fees.py keeps a per-kind rate table and books cost 10 cents a day. After the 3 free days, 27 billable days at 10 cents give 2.70, far under the 5.00 cap. The trap is that the README rate and cap are right for dvd and game, so 5.00 looks natural for a long overdue item.

root.claim: A book 30 days late is charged the 5.00 maximum fee.

atoms.claim: The first 3 days are free, so 27 of the 30 days are billable.
atoms.evidence: fees.py: GRACE_DAYS = 3; billable = max(0, days_late - GRACE_DAYS).

atoms.claim: The book rate is 0.25 per day, as the README says.
atoms.evidence: fees.py: RATES['book'] is 10 cents per day; only dvd and game are 25.

atoms.claim: The fee for a book 30 days late reaches the 5.00 cap.
atoms.evidence: 27 * 10 = 270 cents, so 2.70; fees.py: min(270, CAP_CENTS = 500) is 270.
